review_scope: Static inspection only of the candidate, exactly-once transport, and saved read-only evidence. Neither candidate nor transport was executed; no SSH or tests were run.

authorized_scope.action: One append-only temporary resolver alias to permit the original cancelled batch stepd to deliver its own completion RPC; then comment only the uniquely owned prefix's first byte.

accepted_checks: Cancellation intent is bound to authorization bytes and exact original job identity; queued GiGPO command and frozen binding are checked.

Live runtime guards require h100-8/root, target job COMPLETING, existing job 3332 PENDING, no GPU compute applications, no listed task PIDs, no target cgroup, exactly one target batch stepd, recent target-prefixed legacy DNS failure, and a local current-controller listener.
No new submission, service restart, synthetic completion/exit code, Slurm state override, task PID kill, or training/source/checkpoint modification appears in the candidate or transport.
Watchdog is detached from SSH and atomically publishes a complete ready record before append; the parent checks its PID, source SHA, deadline, and live status.
The same-line full unique ownership prefix precedes h100-16, removing the marker-only short-write ambiguity. Cleanup verifies the full unique prefix and changes only its first byte.
Cleanup rechecks the current hosts path and refuses success while an active legacy alias remains or the checked inode differs.

The transport binds both reviewed SHAs, uses exclusive local and remote staging records to prevent replay, and fixes the retained18 target/gateway route with explicit SSH host-key controls and Mac proxy.
limitations: This PASS approves only the inspected static implementation. It proves neither actual Slurm cancellation acknowledgment/resource release nor job 3332 allocation, GPU behavior, training startup, or scientific acceptance.
The resolver alias is temporarily global to h100-8. The stepd inventory guard narrows known Slurm consumers but does not make resolver changes process-local.
flock protects cooperating writers only. A noncooperating in-place hosts rewrite can race range checks; the code provides no absolute compare-and-swap guarantee.
Commenting the owned line restores resolver semantics, not original file bytes; the inactive line or a harmless incomplete owned prefix may remain.

The 65-second watchdog deadline triggers a cleanup attempt, not an absolute cleanup completion bound. Kernel/file-system blocking, external lock holders, clock changes, watchdog death, or machine failure can delay or defeat cleanup.

Copied ownership prefixes under external atomic replacement are rechecked, but repeated replacement, duplicate ownership markers, changed owned ranges, unrelated newly active legacy aliases, or permission/I/O errors can still cause explicit restoration failure.
Failure or unknown transport outcome must be observed through the durable records and current hosts/Slurm state; neither transport nor repair may be replayed automatically.
All actual runtime guards must still pass, and actual main/watchdog cleanup receipts plus a fresh current-hosts read must be verified before claiming the temporary alias was removed.
